papers.title: Relativistic Dynamical Evolution of Kilonova Spectral Emission
papers.abstract: We develop a relativistic dynamical model for the thermal evolution of expanding kilonova ejecta, in which the effective temperature is determined by the ejecta mass, opacity, velocity, and radioactive heating rate. The resulting thermal evolution follows a broken power law as the ejecta transition from the optically thick to the optically thin regime. We incorporate this thermal history into a relativistic spectral calculation that accounts for the equal-arrival-time surface geometry and Doppler boosting, enabling us to model the observed kilonova spectrum and constrain the underlying ejecta properties. We investigate the effects of the model parameters and relativistic corrections on the observed temperature and spectral shape, and find that light-travel-time delays and Doppler shifts can produce significant spectral distortions at high ejecta velocities. We apply the model to the early-time X-shooter spectrum of the kilonova AT2017gfo and infer the ejecta mass, opacity, and velocity through Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting with a Student's $t$ likelihood. We find that relativistic effects become increasingly important for fast ejecta ($v \gtrsim 0.5c$), particularly at large viewing angles, where the observed temperature can differ substantially from the rest-frame effective temperature. These results highlight the importance of incorporating relativistic and equal-arrival-time effects when interpreting early-time kilonova spectra, especially for rapidly expanding ejecta.

papers.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
papers.abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+δ^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

papers.title: Equivariant Experience Replay for Continual Learning in Imaging Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose Equivariant Experience Replay, a new paradigm for achieving continual learning of deep networks for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Inspired by recent advances on unsupervised learning methods such as equivariant imaging/splitting, we find the exploitation of group-symmetry structure is particularly relevant and effective in continual learning setting for ill-posed inversion tasks. We therefore propose this new experience replay scheme, which is tailored for such inverse problems. Our numerical study demonstrates the superiority of our method compared to existing continual learning methods for inverse problems in medical imaging and image processing.

papers.title: Consistent but Biased: Chair Personas Trade Noise for Bias in Multi-Agent Clinical Decisions
papers.abstract: In clinical systems built from several large language model (LLM) agents, one agent often chairs the discussion and makes the final decision. Whether the chair's persona prompt changes that decision, or the agreement between repeated runs that some systems treat as reliability, has not been tested with the case held constant. We ask whether the persona changes the decision or only its timing, how it affects agreement between runs, and which behaviors appear when the prompt describes only personality traits. A simulated department of seven agents discussed 20 published cases of degenerative cervical myelopathy, with the case reports replayed unchanged in every run. Only the prompts of the chair and its deputy changed (no persona, or a consultative, autocratic or avoidant one), written either as rules of conduct or as personality traits. With personas written as rules, the chair chose to operate now in 93% of runs when autocratic and in 2% when avoidant, against 57% without a persona. Surgery was still planned in nearly all decisions, so the personas mainly changed whether to operate now or after more tests. These effects held with a second model and reworded prompts. The autocratic and avoidant personas made the three runs of a case agree more often, but only about as often as chance predicts, and Fleiss $κ$ did not rise. Prompts that described only personality traits kept more than half of the autocratic and avoidant effects on operating now. They reproduced quick decisions, delays and extra tests, but not ignoring red flags, dropping backup plans or passing the decision to the family. Studies should report and vary the chair's persona as they do the model, and correct agreement between runs for chance before calling it reliability.

papers.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.

papers.title: A Potential New Dimension of Astrophysical Aromatic Functionalization: Phosphaethynyl (CP) Derivatives
papers.abstract: Quantum chemical computations outline a thermodynamically viable, low-temperature, gas-phase formation pathway for phosphaethynyl cyclopropenylidene ($c$-C$_3$HCP), resulting from cyclopropenylidene ($c$-C$_3$H$_2$) and the phosphaethynyl (CP) radical. Given the detections of both $c$-C$_3$H$_2$ and the CP radical toward circumstellar shells along with the provided reaction pathway, $c$-C$_3$HCP is a potentially present astro-molecule which could be searched for in phosphorus rich environments. The reaction of CP and benzene (C$_6$H$_6$) to produce phosphaethynyl benzene (C$_6$H$_5$CP) is also explored. A marginally emerged, but tentative, transition state is identified for this reaction using certain quantum chemical approaches but not others. Consequently, the formation of CP-substituted benzoid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in astrophysical environments from CP + PAH reactions is possible but currently uncertain. Additionally, explicitly correlated coupled cluster quartic force field and second-order vibrational perturbation theory rovibrational analysis of the vibrational frequencies and rotational constants of $c$-C$_3$HCP are provided, as well as density functional theory predictions of the same for CP-benzene (C$_6$H$_5$CP) and both isomers of CP-naphthalene (C$_1$$_0$H$_7$CP). Our results suggest that IR searches for these molecules would likely be unsuccessful due to the low intensities and coincidence with PAH features, but their large dipole moments could make them feasible to detect with radio astronomy. The barrierless formation of $c$-C$_3$HCP and possibly barrierless synthesis of C$_6$H$_5$CP stand as examples for future investigations of other CP-substituted aromatic molecules, marking the potential beginning of a new frontier of astronomical aromatic functionalization.

papers.title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it. Counterfactual branching estimates this credit by re-running the episode after an alternative decision, but the branch draws its sampling noise independently of the factual episode, so the outcome difference mixes the effect of the decision with the luck of everything that follows. We observe that in agentic search the retriever, the corpus, and the grader are deterministic, so an episode is a deterministic function of the policy's decisions and its sampling noise. Twin worlds are therefore realizable: the same noise, a different decision. We introduce TWICE (TWIn-world Credit Estimation), which keys the Gumbel noise of every token by turn and line, rolls out counterfactual twins that inherit the factual episode's downstream noise, and turns their paired outcome differences into turn-level advantages for policy-gradient updates on actor-sampled trajectories; only the actor is deployed. Twin credit is unbiased for any coupling quality, its variance is that of an independent counterfactual scaled by $1-ρ$, where $ρ$ is the twins' outcome correlation, and under coupling the number of rollouts needed to resolve an advantage of size $Δ$ falls from $Θ(Δ^{-2})$ to $Θ(Δ^{-1})$. A square-root rule spends the twin budget where outcomes are predicted to disagree per unit cost. On seven question-answering benchmarks, TWICE improves the average exact match of GRPO by 5.3 and 4.5 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, outperforms tree-search and counterfactual-branching baselines, and uses 68% fewer auxiliary tokens than VinePPO.

papers.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},μ_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

papers.title: Cross-Validation of Infrasound Detections and Fireball Observations from the Global Fireball Observatory
papers.abstract: How do infrasound signals from fireballs relate to atmospheric entry conditions and the physical properties of their parents meteoroids? In this study, we investigate the detectability of infrasound generated by local-to-regional fireballs and use the associated signals to constrain meteoroid physical properties. Across Western Australia and California, the Global Fireball Observatory (GFO) recorded nearly 300 fireball events with well-constrained trajectories within 500 km of an infrasound array over an 11-year period. Of these, 20 fireballs were confidently associated with infrasound detections. For these events, we estimate energies, constrain source altitudes using atmospheric ray-tracing simulations, and investigate source mechanisms using a multi-diagnostic approach. In particular, we examine whether the recorded infrasonic signals originated from cylindrical line sources (ballistic shocks) or discrete fragmentation episodes. Our results show that infrasound-detected fireballs span a broad range of dynamical and physical properties. This variability indicates that infrasound detectability is governed by a combination of source characteristics, atmospheric propagation conditions, and source-receiver geometry, rather than any single entry parameter. Analysis of the fireball shock source mechanisms reveals an even contribution from both ballistic and fragmentation-related sources. These results also demonstrate the value of combining infrasound and optical observations for robust constraints on meteoroid shock generation processes.

papers.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
papers.abstract: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.

papers.title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
papers.abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.

papers.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core
papers.abstract: LLM agents that act on live Web data must combine heterogeneous evidence, remember what they have done and improve from outcomes without weakening their own safeguards. We study this problem in autonomous investing, where every action is irreversible and based on untrusted Web content. We present Steward, a multi-agent LLM system that draws the boundary of self-evolution in its type system. First, nine role-specialised agents decide jointly: four analysts read news feeds, SEC filings, macroeconomic series and market data and emit typed reports, from which a Portfolio Manager sets target positions that a protected Risk Manager audits. Second, a seven-layer shared memory, assembled by code from the system's own record, gives each decision its position context, the market narrative, calibration and the agent's past decisions. Third, the system improves itself by review: code grades every trade and forecast nightly and writes the grades into memory, and each quarter a reflector proposes prompt learnings that a deterministic gate applies reversibly and replay of recorded inputs verifies. All three operate around an invariant core of order arithmetic, risk rules and discipline-agent prompts that no self-edit can reach. In a five-month live deployment (102 trading days, 1,632 LLM calls), the system contained a 24.6% sector drawdown to a 0.3% loss; in replay of its recorded inputs, a single model given the same raw data traded more and lost 1.35 points against the market over five days where the joint design showed no significant loss, and no injected instruction was followed; and a 2015-2026 backtest shows the core alone lowering the maximum drawdown under all 50 random entry policies. The reflector traced the dominant failure to its root cause, and the gate applied a learning that the agent adopted on trigger evenings and on no control evening. Code: https://github.com/yebof/quant-agent

papers.title: CODI: Improving Self-Supervised Vision Transformers with Cross Distillation
papers.abstract: Self-supervised Vision Transformers learn strong image-level representations, but their patch-level representations can be unreliable for dense prediction. We study this mismatch and find that the class token concentrates global semantics on a small number of representative patches, while dense prediction errors often occur on low-attention regions. We provide a local gradient analysis showing that, along the [CLS] attention readout, image-level self-distillation gradients are weighted by [CLS]-to-patch attention mass. To provide masked patches with global semantics without changing the architecture, we propose Cross Distillation (CODI), which mixes a small amount of the teacher class-token distribution into each teacher patch-token target. CODI gives every masked patch an attention-independent semantic correction while preserving the standard self-distillation architecture. Experiments on dense and image-level benchmarks show that CODI improves both dense and image-level performance under aligned pretraining settings. Code is available at https://github.com/EldercatSAM/CODI.

papers.title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.

papers.title: GSHeadRelight: Fast Relightability for 3D Gaussian Head Synthesis
papers.abstract: Relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits are essential in applications such as portrait photography, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). Despite recent progress, 3D-aware portrait relighting remains challenging due to the demands for photorealistic rendering, real-time performance, and generalization to unseen subjects. Existing works either rely on supervision from limited and expensive light stage captured data or produce suboptimal results. Moreover, many works are based on generative NeRFs, which suffer from poor 3D consistency and low real-time performance. We resort to recent progress on generative 3D Gaussians and design a lighting model based on a unified neural radiance transfer representation, which responds linearly to incident light. Using only in-the-wild images, our method achieves state-of-the-art relighting results and a significantly faster rendering speed ($\times12$) compared to previous 3D-aware portrait relighting research. Project page: http://www.geometrylearning.com/GSHeadRelight/.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Modeling of Deformation-Based Pinching Antennas
papers.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PAS) rely on local perturbations of a guiding structure to radiate part of the guided electromagnetic energy, making the physical response of the resulting pinching antenna (PA) fundamental to both guided-wave propagation and free-space radiation. To capture this coupled behavior, we develop an electromagnetic model of a finite deformation-based PA that directly relates the applied waveguide perturbation to its complex reflection and transmission responses and three-dimensional radiation characteristics. Full-wave MEEP simulations validate the model and demonstrate how the pinching ratio and pinched-section length jointly affect the transmitted power and phase, radiation power-fraction, and radiation pattern, thereby establishing PA geometry as a degree of freedom for controlling the radiation response. Importantly, this geometric dependence extends to communication performance, as the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) results reveal that neither minimizing the PA--user distance nor maximizing the radiation power-fraction necessarily yields the highest SNR, since the applied perturbation also determines the realized gain toward the user.

papers.title: Sketching Outside the Hilbert Space for the Infinite-Dimensional Randomised SVD
papers.abstract: In randomised numerical linear algebra, common choices for distributions of sketch vectors $ω\in \mathbb R^n$ are isotropic, so that $\mathbb E[ωω^T]=I_n$. Unfortunately, the natural extension of an isotropic vector in $(\mathbb R^n, \|\cdot \|_{2})$ to an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ may not exist as an element of the space, posing an obstacle for any attempt to lift the randomised SVD to infinite-dimensional target operators $A$. Current workarounds either forego isotropy and take $ω$ to be a continuous Gaussian process with trace-class covariance operators, or leave $ω$ implicit by instead sampling $Aω$ as if $ω$ were isotropic Gaussian. We unify their approaches by introducing "sketch functionals", an example of cylindrical random variables (Vakhania--Tarieladze--Chobanyan 1987) which allow us to treat general, non-Gaussian distributions with bounded covariance operators. To demonstrate the utility of the new theory, we apply it to develop novel bounds for the infinite-dimensional randomised SVD with a general class of sub-Gaussian sketch distributions.

papers.title: Shift-aware score transport for privacy auditing without retraining
papers.abstract: Privacy auditing empirically assesses privacy leakage by using membership inference attacks to establish lower bounds on privacy loss. We consider an observational auditing setting in which the auditor cannot insert canaries, control data inclusion, or retrain the target model, and must instead rely on fixed sets of known members and non-members. This setting is relevant for large deployed models or when retraining is restricted by computational or access constraints. In this case, non-members available for auditing may differ in distribution from the training data, causing membership-inference scores to be skewed due to the distribution shift. We address this problem by estimating the counterfactual in-distribution non-member score distribution using the available out-of-distribution (OOD) non-members. Our proposed method learns the relationship between data representations and membership-inference scores from OOD non-members and transports it to the target covariate distribution. Because this transport may become unreliable under extrapolation or imperfect conditional invariance, we further introduce a conservative correction calibrated directly to the nominal transported privacy level. We construct controlled calibration tasks from the available non-member data to estimate how representation-space displacement inflates the audit, and use this estimate to correct the transport-induced audit error. Across multiple datasets with distribution shifts, our method yields substantially more stable privacy estimates while retaining tighter lower bounds than baselines.

papers.title: Decentralized Bi-Level Optimization for Cooperative Orbital Transportation of a Rigid Payload
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of the space economy, alongside increasing orbital congestion and debris, is driving demand for reliable on-orbit transportation of large and non-cooperative objects. Performing such transportation with a swarm of small spacecraft distributes risk and removes the single point of failure inherent to monolithic architectures, but requires solving a non-convex trajectory optimization coupling every agent's cone-constrained thrust to the payload's rotational dynamics. Existing approaches span decentralized control laws with asymptotic guarantees but limited constraint enforcement, and centralized and partially centralized planners that reintroduce a single point of failure. In this work, we present a decentralized bi-level framework driven by exact gradients: the problem is split into an inner convex thrust allocation and an outer search over payload torque trajectories. This decomposition yields fuel-efficient solutions quickly, without requiring full NLP convergence, and at short timescales its performance scales with the number of agents. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established, and the method is validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulation, including closed-loop recovery from in-flight faults. These properties make the framework well suited to spacecraft swarm applications.

papers.title: Measuring the Reasoning-Action Coupling in Driving Vision-Language-Action Models through Counterfactuals
papers.abstract: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models bring an appealing form of explainability to a safety-critical domain, since a system that can state the reasons for its maneuvers offers the transparency that deployment and public trust in autonomous driving demand. These models read the world into language before they act on it, describing the scene and reasoning over it in text that ranges from chain-of-thought to multi-stage question answering on the way to a trajectory. That framing quietly assumes two separable properties, namely that the trajectory follows the generated reasoning and that the generated reasoning tracks the causes that actually produce the trajectory. To thoroughly investigate these properties, we apply causal, counterfactual interventions to four driving VLAs across different benchmarks. First, we perturb the models' own reasoning and show that altering its meaning produces small trajectory changes relative to blanking the same models' camera inputs, a pattern that persists across benchmarks and model architectures. We then construct scene-level counterfactuals through photorealistic removal of key objects named in the models' reasoning and analyze whether the generated reasoning and trajectories track these changes. Overall, our findings indicate that the reasoning these models present to account for their resulting driving behavior is weakly coupled to that behavior itself, pointing to limits on the explainability these systems are intended to provide.

papers.title: Evaluating Type-1 Diabetes Digital Twins by Decision Quality
papers.abstract: A digital twin (DT) for type 1 diabetes (T1D) can predict how an individual's blood glucose will respond to different insulin treatments without actually trying them. For each treatment, downstream statistics of predicted glucose trajectories, such as glycemic risk, can be computed to guide clinical decisions. However, the quality of DTs is usually measured by the accuracy of their predicted glucose trajectories, which may not reflect the quality of the downstream treatment decisions they inform. In this work, we directly evaluate DTs by this decision quality on downstream treatment ranking, i.e., whether a DT predicts glucose trajectories that can be used to rank candidate treatments as the real patient would. We present an evaluation protocol over 30 virtual patients from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova model, each simulated under 21 different basal-bolus treatments. For each patient, a DT is fitted under one treatment and then produces glucose trajectories for the remaining 20 treatments. Our results show that prediction accuracy and decision quality disagree. A baseline that models the average patient, never seeing the individual's glucose data, has the lowest prediction accuracy of all six methods (RMSE: 63.6 mg/dL) but ranks treatments with the second-highest mean Spearman (0.766), while a black-box neural network that predicts glucose nearly twice as accurately (RMSE: 32.9 mg/dL) ranks them no better than a random ordering of the 20 treatments (0.049 Spearman). Therefore, selecting a DT based on prediction accuracy alone can prefer one that recommends treatments at chance, and decision quality must be evaluated directly rather than assumed to follow from prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that there exist exotic spheres with metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature in infinitely many dimensions: in every dimension $n\equiv3\pmod4$ with $n\geq11$ and $n\not\equiv255\pmod{256}$. Previously, every known closed simply connected manifold of positive sectional curvature in a dimension above $24$ was diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space. The spheres we consider are certain homotopy spheres arising as quotients of special $S^3$-$S^3$ bundles introduced by Sperança. These homotopy spheres are determined by an orthogonal representation $ρ$ of $S^3$ and an $S^3$-conjugation-equivariant map $β$, and are denoted $Σ_{ρ,β}$. By recent constructions, such spheres admit Riemannian metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature. In this paper we consider the spheres $Σ_{ρ_b,β}$ of dimension $4b+3$, $b\geq2$, where $ρ_b$ is the representation of $S^3$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathbb{H}^b$ by left multiplication on the second summand. For these spheres, we show that the Eells-Kuiper invariant is the product of an integer $k(β)$ depending only on $β$ and a rational number $r_b$ given by one coefficient of a power series built from the $\hat A$- and $L$-genera. We then show that, for every $b\geq2$ with $b\not\equiv63\pmod{64}$, there is a map $β$ for which the Eells-Kuiper invariant does not vanish, and thus the corresponding sphere is exotic. A computer calculation also gives the dimensions $n\equiv255\pmod{256}$ below $2^{16}$.

papers.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
papers.abstract: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.

papers.title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
papers.abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning
papers.abstract: Domain generalization (DG) aims to improve the generalization of the model to any unseen domains. Targeting this goal, existing DG methods mainly focus on learning domain-invariant features or prompts from the given source domains. However, these methods rely on source-domain data, and collecting and annotating large-scale single- or multi-source datasets is often infeasible, limiting the practical applicability of DG. To tackle this challenge, we propose {\underline{Do}}main \underline{P}rompt Learning (DoP), a method built on a large vision-language model (e.g., CLIP) for zero-shot domain generalization, which recognizes unseen classes in unseen target domains without access to source-domain data. DoP essentially learns the target domain knowledge via prompt both in text and visual modalities to overcome the domain shift in text-visual modalities under the test-time adaptation formulation. Specifically, DoP first takes text domain learning (TDL) to simulate various distribution shifts by learning diverse style tokens implicitly in the text space with inter-style diversity loss and intra-style consistency loss. Subsequently, DoP employs visual domain learning (VDL) to further refine the target-domain-relevant style token generated by TDL by making use of the test visual data with self-supervised learning. Extensive experiments on popular DG benchmark datasets (e.g., PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and DomainNet) and ImageNet show that our DoP consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art DG approaches. Codes are available at: https://github.com/shiming-chen/DoP.

papers.title: On Modified Newton Methods for Unconstrained Optimization Based on Lanczos Tridiagonalization
papers.abstract: For a strongly convex unconstrained minimization problem, Newton's method with a line search offers rapid convergence to a minimizer by incorporating second-order information. However, for a general unconstrained problem the Hessian need not be positive definite, which can lead to the inability to find a search direction or to search directions that fail to produce descent. Modified Newton methods are designed to handle this situation. This paper considers modifications to a Newton-conjugate-gradient approach based on Lanczos tridiagonalization. Existing methods are extended using dynamic modification schemes that provide a descent direction while keeping the modification bounded. A Lanczos-based scheme and a conjugate-gradient (CG)-based scheme are formulated and analyzed. These methods are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, but their practical behavior differs in finite precision. Finally, it is shown how the convergence and computational cost are affected by varying the amount of additional curvature introduced and by allowing the early termination of the inner iterations.

papers.title: Impacts of generative AI skill development on academic adaptation and learning outcomes among university students
papers.abstract: Understanding how university students perceive the development of their generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) skills over time can clarify how GenAI use relates to learning and academic outcomes. This study examined perceived skill-development trajectories, changes in learning practices, and associated academic gains using a retrospective questionnaire with 313 analyzed responses and interviews with 18 students across subject areas. Descriptive and comparative analyses and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were integrated with thematic analysis. Perceived developmental trajectories were heterogeneous: 34.2% of students reported rapid early improvement followed by a plateau, 28.4% steady improvement, and 21.1% delayed acceleration. Development was also uneven across skills, with improvement in evaluating GenAI outputs perceived as more challenging; assignments were the most frequently selected driver of skill growth. Interviews further indicated increasingly specific prompting, tailored verification, and selective delegation, although some students reported stable routines, dependence, skipped reasoning, or improvements attributable partly to better GenAI tools. Academic gains were reported more often for assignments than for examinations. The SEM indicated a positive indirect association between perceived skill growth and academic gains through adaptation of assignment processes, whereas academic gains did not clearly differ across developmental trajectory groups after multiplicity correction. The findings suggest that perceived GenAI skill development varies in both trajectory and skill domain and is associated with changes in learning practices and differentiated academic benefits.

papers.title: AstroBench: Benchmarking Free-Floating Capture and Space Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Capturing a loose object inside a spacecraft requires a robot to approach a target that can translate and rotate, and whose motion changes when contact is made. These conditions motivate evaluation beyond manipulation of supported objects. We introduce AstroBench, an open benchmark for free-floating capture and space robotic manipulation with a fixed-base arm. The task suite combines four initial-motion tracks with sample-storage operations based on MELFI hardware and cap and captive-screw servicing based on the Robotic Refueling Mission. The two workcells provide nine task definitions and 29 task-target combinations. A metadata-filtered Objaverse inventory supplies 8,414 object instances for asset expansion, alongside five cabin visual contexts and versioned task instructions. We report two acquisition-focused experiments using existing checkpoints. A frozen $π_{0.5}$ DROID joint-position policy captures 2 of 200 static targets and 4 of 200 moving targets across twenty object identities. A cube-specific ACT policy captures 8 of 10 static targets and 6 of 10 moving targets in a separate experiment. Each experiment retains its recorded observation, action and capture configuration. The results document difficult direct transfer for the tested generalist checkpoint and successful task-specific capture behavior, while identifying concrete settings for studying motion-aware perception and contact-sensitive control. Code, task definitions and editable workcell assets are available at https://github.com/AstroUpLab/AstroBench.

papers.title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
papers.abstract: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system. While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. With the recent advent of X-ray polarimetric observations enabled by the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), indications of a possible misalignment of the neutron star rotational axis with respect to the binary axis have been reported. Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission. We compare our results with those for aligned systems. Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with IXPE and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

papers.title: Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks: Enhancing Flexibility in Node Dependencies via penalized B-Splines
papers.abstract: Bayesian networks for continuous variables often rely on restrictive assumptions: linear Gaussian models lack flexibility to capture nonlinear dependencies, while non-parametric approaches provide greater flexibility at a high computational cost. This creates a gap for modeling scenarios where variables are approximately Gaussian but exhibit nonlinear relationships. We introduce Semi-Linear Gaussian Bayesian Networks (SLGBN), a novel class of continuous Bayesian networks designed to bridge this gap, preserving Gaussian conditional distributions while introducing nonlinear conditional mean functions. The proposed framework provides a unified probabilistic framework combining linear Gaussian and nonlinear Gaussian conditional models within the same Bayesian network Nonlinear conditional mean functions are estimated using generalized additive models (GAMs) with penalized B-splines. We present parameter estimation procedures for both types of nodes, as well as a greedy hill-climbing algorithm for learning the network structure under the SLGBN framework. To assess its performance, we compare SLGBN with other continuous Bayesian network models, including semiparametric Bayesian networks (SPBN) and Linear Gaussian Bayesian networks (LGBN). Experimental results evaluate both goodness of fit and the ability to recover the underlying network structure. The results show that, in the presence of nonlinear Gaussian relationships, SLGBN achieves better fit and improved structure recovery compared to alternative models, particularly when combined with the Extended Bayesian Information Criterion (EBIC*) score. Furthermore, by retaining Gaussian conditional distributions, SLGBN offers computational advantages over fully semiparametric approaches.

papers.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$. The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $ν=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $ν\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $ν\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $ν\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.

papers.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.

papers.title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
papers.abstract: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm^3 N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = Lσ/(ωε0εh), here, σ conductivity, ω - cyclic frequency, εh,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.

authors.name: Massimiliano Zamengo
authors.institution: Research Organization of Information and Systems

papers.title: AI Risk Ontologies for the EU AI Act Compliance: AIRO, VAIR, and their Integration with DPV
papers.abstract: As the use of AI, and consequently its harms, becomes more prevalent, the global discourse around AI has become increasingly risk-aware. With new risks emerging more frequently than ever, a key challenge is how to represent, document, and catalogue AI risks in an effective, interoperable, and queryable manner. Additionally, the European Union (EU) AI Act's requirements for "high-risk" AI systems to manage and document the risks creates the need for open and interoperable tools, methods, and standards that facilitate AI risk management in an ever-changing environment. In this paper, we present ontologies and taxonomies developed to assist with risk management and documentation, in line with the requirements of the EU the AI Act. We developed the AI Risk Ontology (AIRO) to specify AI use cases and their associated risks, complemented by the Vocabulary of AI Risks (VAIR), which populates AIRO with taxonomies of concepts. Key international standards on AI and risk, namely ISO/IEC 23894 on AI risk management and ISO/IEC 22989 on AI terminology informed the development of the ontologies. To promote reuse and enable multi-regulatory compliance, AIRO and VAIR have been integrated in the Data Privacy Vocabulary (DPV) through a consensus-building process, expanding DPV's scope from data to AI.

papers.title: Analysis of a coronal hole jet in the chromosphere and the transition region with IRIS data and SDO observations
papers.abstract: Coronal jets are transient phenomena that occur throughout the solar atmosphere, often triggered by the activation of mini-filaments. Jets are an important field of study, as they are believed to contribute to the mass supply of the solar wind. We study a small-scale solar jet occurring in a low-latitude coronal hole, focusing on traces of the jet eruption to the lower atmosphere, utilizing chromospheric and transition region diagnostics. We also investigate the possible mechanisms and dynamic conditions leading to its onset. We analyze ultraviolet spectra from the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph to investigate chromospheric dynamics and their connection to the transition region, using diagnostics of the Mg II k 2796.35 Å and Si IV 1393.75 Å lines, together with non-LTE inversions. We complement this analysis with multiwavelength imaging and magnetograms from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, as well as magnetic field modeling. The analysis of Mg II k and Si IV parameters reveals a coupling between chromospheric and transition region plasma dynamics. Profiles on the jet spire present deeper central reversals, larger peak separations and higher transition region Doppler velocities. The jet initiation is associated with a mini-filament-like structure, preceded by dynamic variations in the photospheric magnetic field. We find single-peaked Mg II k profiles at one of its footpoints, possibly indicating plasma drainage. The presence of a null point and a quasi-separatrix layer suggests that reconnection can play a role in the mini-filament-like structure destabilization and jet eruption. This study suggests that the signature and possibly the origin of coronal jets can be traced down to the chromosphere. The detailed analysis of the Mg II k profiles at the jet spire and the mini-filament-like structure may provide valuable observational constraints for future MHD simulations.

papers.title: Photometric classification and out-of-taxonomy detection of ZTF transients with FLARE
papers.abstract: Photometric classifiers decide which of the million nightly alerts of time-domain surveys receive one of the few thousand spectra taken each year, and they are the first place where a transient outside the trained classes can be noticed. We present flare, the photometric classification and anomaly-detection module of AppleCiDEr, evaluated on 10 497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients in six classes and 53 objects from families outside the taxonomy. Catalogue context raises the macro F1 score, with the largest gains where the defining information is absent from the light curve. Blind detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy objects at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated review loop recovers 83% of them after inspecting 15% of the stream. The first confirmations of a new family are most useful in the feature space: with the same eleven labels, a head on the frozen features detects 68% of the tidal disruption events hidden from the training against 57% for a combiner over the anomaly scores, and retraining with them as a new class reaches 85%. The module runs in production on Fritz, the ZTF instance of SkyPortal, and its alarm is reported as a false-alarm rate per unit time on the stream, calibrated on the photometry that the service receives

authors.name: Xuanrui Zhang
authors.institution: Hebei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Gravitational Lensing of the Bullet Cluster in the CCC+TL Cosmology: A Controlled Proof-of-Concept Study
papers.abstract: A proof-of-concept study of gravitational lensing in the Bullet Cluster under Covarying Coupling Constants plus Tired Light (CCC+TL) cosmology. Using a JWST spectroscopic catalogue of 219 cluster members and 135 gold multiple images in 49 systems from Rihtarsic et al. (2026), we construct convergence maps for CCC+TL and a simplified $Λ$CDM model using their respective angular-diameter distances and critical surface densities. The CCC+TL model adopts a two-parameter effective-density prescription anchored to the same virial-scale mass budget as $Λ$CDM, rather than fitted to multiple-image positions. The CCC+TL and $Λ$CDM mean-convergence bands in radial rings overlap within the propagated $\pm 30 \%$ virial-mass uncertainty across all rings containing multiple images ($θ\leq80\arcsec$). On a source-plane back-projection diagnostic ($α_{\mathrm{phys}}(z_s)=α_{\mathrm{dft}}\timesβ(z_s)/β(z_{s,\mathrm{ref}})$ with $z_{s,\mathrm{ref}}=2$), the unoptimised two-parameter CCC+TL pipeline yields $\mathrm{RMS}=5.22\arcsec$ ($4.63\arcsec$--$5.91\arcsec$), compared with $6.82\arcsec$ ($5.75\arcsec$--$8.09\arcsec$) for the $Λ$CDM reference. The optimised 32-parameter Lenstool reconstruction achieves an image-plane RMS of $\sim\!0.41\arcsec$, which is not directly comparable to these source-plane values. Within the $\pm 30\%$ $M_{200}$ uncertainty band, the source-plane scatter ranges partially overlap. The CCC+TL effective extra-gravity distribution follows the galaxy distribution rather than X-ray gas, reproducing the qualitative morphology of the Bullet Cluster, though this agreement is partly structural as profiles center on member galaxies by construction. For the same mass, Einstein-radius scaling differs by only 1.7% between cosmologies. These results are a necessary first step toward a full image-plane likelihood test of CCC+TL.

papers.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
papers.abstract: Accuracy on medical examinations is common evidence offered for the clinical use of language models, yet a health system that intends to run an open model on its own hardware needs to know considerably more: whether the model recognizes when it is likely to be wrong, whether medical fine-tuning improves this ability, whether its correct answers rest on sound clinical reasoning, or whether it actually uses the images it is given. We examine these questions for four open models of 8 to 27 billion parameters on the Spanish MIR residency examination, scoring 1,552 questions from eight editions under the exam's own rules. Answering every question, the three larger models would rank among roughly the first 600 to 3,000 candidates, with 41 to 43 specialties still open to them. Abstention, however, never pays, because even their least confident answers are right more often than the 25% break-even. Medical fine-tuning reduced overconfidence at the cost of accuracy, without improving how well confidence separates right from wrong answers. Moreover, 13-38% of correct answers rejected a distractor for a clinically unsound reason that confidence did not reflect, and removing or swapping the provided contextual images left accuracy unchanged.

papers.title: The Psychology of an AI Hacker
papers.abstract: Human hackers rely on composure, persistence, vigilance, and confidence under pressure. We investigate whether analogous emotion representations in AI models can improve cybersecurity AI performance. Using CT0, a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer released as alias3-micro, we extract 171 emotion directions from its residual stream without retraining and evaluate steering interventions on cybench-subtask across 415 campaigns. Steering toward calm, serene, or desperate improves performance by 1.6 to 2.1 percentage points across ten seeds, while other emotions show limited or negative effects. Results depend strongly on steering direction, layer, and intensity. We further introduce a lightweight context-aware router that selects emotion directions dynamically during execution. With approximately 80 ms decision overhead per request, this approach improves performance by 4.2 percentage points across ten seeds, outperforming fixed steering and achieving a positive 95% confidence interval. These findings suggest that emotion representations in language models are measurable, controllable, and useful for adaptive cybersecurity reasoning.

papers.title: BelT Block Cipher
papers.abstract: BelT is a block cipher with a 128-bit block size and a 256-bit key, developed in Belarus and adopted as part of the Belarusian national standard STB 34.101.31 for encryption and integrity control. Its specification was issued as a preliminary standard in 2007, becoming a final standard in 2011. BelT employs an eight-round structure combining elements of a Feistel network and the Lai-Massey scheme. This paper presents a complete description of the cipher and explains the principles underlying its design. Software performance and possible optimizations of BelT are discussed in comparison with those of candidates in the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) competition.

papers.title: HeyGen Voice: Scene-Aware Voice Cloning for Talking Videos
papers.abstract: Most voice-cloning systems are built for audio alone: they copy the reference recording's delivery and acoustics, so a voice cloned on a phone sounds like a phone recording whether the speaker is pictured in a studio, on a street, or in a cathedral. Speech for a talking video should sound like the pictured person speaking in the pictured place. We present HeyGen Voice, a scene-aware voice-cloning model that separates who is speaking from how and where: it keeps the speaker's voice from an everyday recording while the target image sets the delivery and acoustics. Prior image-conditioned TTS does half of this job: it either adds scene acoustics without keeping a specific speaker or infers a voice from a face. HeyGen Voice is a multimodal autoregressive transformer conditioned on the image, speaker and scene captions, and the voice recording, trained in five stages that move from multilingual TTS pretraining through simulated and real cross-scene adaptation to reinforcement and preference optimization. Two clone policies trade scene adaptation against fidelity to the original recording, and an audio anchor holds long scripts in one voice and one acoustic environment. Listeners prefer HeyGen Voice over leading commercial systems across a third-party arena, production votes, and talking-video studies: it ranks first (Elo 1201) on the public Artificial Analysis controlled-voice TTS leaderboard (October 2026); in a blind test, users cloning their own voice chose it over ElevenLabs v4 and Cartesia Sonic 3.6 in 62% and 54% of votes; and volunteers rated talking videos of their own digital twin about 10 to 30 points higher (out of 100) when voiced by HeyGen Voice than by leading commercial alternatives. Try HeyGen Voice and hear samples at https://heygen.com/heygen-voice.

papers.title: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation
papers.abstract: Recent large reasoning models can infer where ordinary photos were taken using only visual information, creating a serious location privacy risk even when metadata and obvious geographic identifiers are removed. To understand the mechanism behind such fine-grained localization, we develop GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that exposes how models extract location-relevant visual clues and compose them through coarse-to-fine geographic reasoning. We evaluate GeoTrace on a worldwide benchmark of 525 ordinary images spanning natural, urban, residential, and human-centered scenes while excluding famous landmarks and direct location indicators. Our results show that GeoTrace localizes 25.71% of images within 1 km with Gemini-3-Flash and 16.95% with GPT-5-mini. More importantly, our analysis reveals a key insight in the visual clue chain: broad scene properties mainly support coarse localization, whereas precise localization disproportionately relies on small, distinctive, and editable local clues. Building on this insight, we develop GeoShift, a proactive user-side defense that breaks the visual clue chain before image release. Rather than simply removing geographic evidence, GeoShift preserves stable scene properties, selects a visually compatible false target location, and strategically rewrites high-impact geo-revealing clues to construct a coherent alternative geographic hypothesis. Experiments show that GeoShift reduces street-level localization from 16.95% to 2.48% under GPT-5-mini and from 25.71% to 3.81% under Gemini-3-Flash, while preserving visual quality and remaining effective against adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Co^2Gen: Collaboratively Generating Task Plans for Decentralized Multi-Robot and Human Collaboration
papers.abstract: Visual Language Action (VLA) models are designed to be generalist robot models that can be implemented across embodiments, tasks and environments. However, their ability to collaborate with other robots and humans remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a framework to automate the generation of multi-robot collaborative data for decentralized VLA training without requiring human teleoperation. Our framework first utilizes a decentralized collaborative planning approach to generate multi-robot collaborative robot plans in the form of an executable function. We then utilize the collaborative plan to produce collaborative demonstration data to finetune VLA models in a decentralized manner. We show that our approach produces demonstration data that when used to finetune VLA models on decentralized collaboration tasks matches the task performance of VLA models finetuned on human-teleoperated collaborative data.
