papers.title: Rematching Estimators for Average Treatment Effects
papers.abstract: Matching estimators are widely applied in practice for their great intuitive appeal. However, simple matching estimators with a fixed number of matches ($M_0$) are generally inefficient. In this article, we propose matching estimators with a variable number of matches to gain efficiency via rematching. Rather than increasing $M_0$ to gain precision, which introduces an increase in bias, the key is to rematch the treated units from the opposite direction to utilize unmatched control units. Our rematching estimators are applicable to both the average treatment effect and its counterpart for the treated population. The proposed rematching estimators are proven asymptotically valid and uniformly more efficient than matching estimators with the same $M_0$. Simulation results confirm that the proposed rematching estimators substantially improve the simple matching estimators in finite samples. As an empirical illustration, we apply the estimators proposed in this article to the National Supported Work data.

papers.title: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Financial news can influence investment decisions long after publication. Timely news may reach an investor before prices fully adjust, whereas older news may already be reflected in prices. We examine two ways to handle aging signals: retain them and give a portfolio policy timing information, or filter them out before portfolio selection. A fixed large language model (LLM) extracts signals from public SEC disclosures. We compare these treatments in reinforcement learning (RL) policies and LLMs that choose portfolios directly. We evaluate returns after trading costs in historical tests over 2023-2025. RL choices respond to timing information in a controlled test, but historical returns show no consistent benefit from adding it. For the LLM, filtering old news produced the highest average net return, reaching 18.43% per year when news delivery was delayed by four weeks. This exceeded the returns of all RL strategies that used news.

papers.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part I: A Compactness Criterion and the Linear Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper and its companion Part II prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. In this first part we prove two ingredients. One is a compactness criterion: for a radial datum, a sequence of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric solutions with converging data, whose non-radial moment is bounded below at some bounded time, has a subsequence converging to a second distinct renormalized weak solution. The other is the linear analysis for the building blocks of our multiscale datum. We show that the linearization of the Euler equations around the basic building block plus a small point vortex has an unstable eigenvalue in a space of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric perturbations. This latter argument depends on rigorous interval arithmetic that we discuss more fully in Part II.

papers.title: Estimating Group Average Treatment Effects in High-Risk Populations with Unobserved Target Membership
papers.abstract: Estimating treatment effects within a prespecified high-risk population is challenging. When risk status is unobserved or the target population is small, analyses restricted to high-risk individuals can be unstable or inefficient. We propose a risk-score-weighted soft-targeting (RSW) estimator for group average treatment effects in high-risk populations. It accommodates two settings: when high-risk status is observed, the membership probability can be estimated within the analysis sample; when unobserved, it can be obtained from a reference model using covariates in the analysis sample. RSW uses these probabilities to represent the target population, learns a doubly robust treatment effect in the full sample, and aggregates a low-dimensional treatment-effect surface over the risk-weighted target distribution. We establish pointwise asymptotic normality and an influence-function-based variance estimator. In simulations with continuous and binary outcomes, RSW had similar bias and lower variance than two hard-targeting alternatives. Sensitivity analyses showed that the gain persisted when treatment-effect sufficiency was violated, although RSW bias increased under strong violations. We applied the method to the All of Us study to estimate effects of non-GLP antidiabetic and antihypertensive medication use on mild cognitive impairment (MCI)-free time restricted at 48 months within comorbidity-defined high-risk subgroups. We estimated the risk score in a nonoverlapping internal reference sample and applied it to the outcome-analysis sample. This illustrates how soft targeting can improve precision while retaining an interpretable high-risk target population.

papers.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
papers.abstract: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

papers.title: DRILL: Training World Models to Improve Policies, Not Predict Pixels
papers.abstract: World models are increasingly used to reduce environment interaction when post-training vision-language-action (VLA) policies with reinforcement learning. Yet they are typically trained to predict pixels one step ahead, even though their role here is not merely to render visually faithful videos but to produce learning signals from imagined rollouts that improve the policy. We show that this mismatch is substantial: lower pixel MSE can produce worse policy gradients, and a world model trained for policy utility can yield better downstream policies despite 17% higher pixel MSE on the next frame. We propose the Downstream-Return Imagination Learning Loop (DRILL), a bilevel framework that updates the world model to maximize the policy's return after an inner GRPO update on imagined rollouts. DRILL has two instantiations. DRILL-VWI is a closed-form surrogate, requiring no additional simulator rollouts, that reweights prediction errors by policy visitation, the group-relative GRPO advantage, and model confidence. DRILL-IMG is a full meta-gradient method that differentiates through the inner update using truncated Hessian-vector products. We show that DRILL-VWI recovers the local one-step component of the DRILL-IMG meta-gradient under score-compatibility and small-residual assumptions. Across five manipulation simulators and two VLA backbones, DRILL-IMG raises mean success rate by 13.1 points over WMPO and 7.9 points over RLVR-World, and complements RLVR pretraining rather than competing with it. More broadly, we believe video world models for VLA reinforcement learning can be productively trained by the policy gradients they produce, not only by pixel-level prediction.

papers.title: Music Between Two Minds: Individual Signatures, Shared States, and the Emergence of Creative Interaction
papers.abstract: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown. Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes. Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos. Improvising pairs thus neither fuse into one system nor remain two independent ones: they preserve individual melodic voices while sharing a rhythmic state, within which moment-to-moment push-pull continually rebalances their interaction. Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

papers.title: Modulation theory of Y- and X-wave Kadomtsev--Petviashvili solitons
papers.abstract: The evolution of long wavelength perturbations of traveling wave 2-soliton solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP) equation are investigated using modulation theory. An initial-boundary value problem for a system of hyperbolic conservation laws is formulated for amplitude and slope perturbations to soliton legs of the resonant (Y-shaped) and X-shaped KP traveling wave solutions. The vertex where individuated soliton legs coalesce is modeled as a moving free boundary where information between the soliton legs can pass. The linearized hyperbolic system is proven to be well-posed under suitable initial conditions and is solved exactly. In the case of the resonant Y-shaped soliton, all admissible simple (rarefaction) waves of the nonlinear system are characterized. Specific perturbations of Y-waves can lead to the dimensionality of the modulated solution changing, corresponding to a physical geometric change to the multi-soliton pattern. Spontaneous leg deletion and leg creation can occur. The conditions under which the Y-wave modulation system can experience gradient catastrophe are given. Gradient catastrophe is regularized by the formation of a new leg, with an augmented modulation system proposed to describe the growth of the new leg. On the other hand, the X-wave system can be reduced to two independent line soliton modulation systems. These findings reinforce the prevalence and generality of resonant Y-shaped vertices in the KP II system and applications.The theoretical modulation predictions are supported by direct numerical simulations of KP II, which show good agreement with the analysis.

papers.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
papers.abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

papers.title: Contestable Agents for Data Governance: Recording Human Stewardship of AI-Generated Metadata Across Structured and Unstructured Systems
papers.abstract: Industrial organizations hold operational knowledge in structured records, such as telemetry, point lists, and transactions, and in unstructured sources, such as manuals, service notes, communications, and inspection reports. Governance programs often manage these sources separately. Classifying, linking, and documenting them depends on a small group of employees with deep domain knowledge. Agents built on large language models can propose metadata, cite documents, and flag quality issues, but unreviewed proposals can spread errors into downstream systems. A perfunctory approval leaves no record of what a reviewer checked. We present contestable governance: specialist agents produce scored, cited arguments for disputed metadata decisions; a steward can accept, reject, modify, or add arguments before commit; and a governance record retains the evidence, interventions, and outcome. A versioned domain glossary supplies model-specific terms and acronym definitions to the agents. We describe the workflow, a triage path that reserves full argumentation for uncertain proposals while preserving review before commit, the scoring and record models, and a gate that controls which verified decisions become precedent. Two HVAC use cases illustrate the pattern: point classification using Brick Schema class labels, supported by an open reference implementation, and an illustrative warranty failure-mode decision linking claim fields and telemetry to service notes and revisioned bulletins.

papers.title: Shear-induced mechanical yielding controls cluster morphology and dynamics in aggregating non-Brownian suspensions
papers.abstract: In sheared aggregating suspensions, flow drives both the formation and breakage of particle clusters, whose dynamic evolution influences transport and rheological properties. Understanding these mechanisms remains challenging due to the complex interplay between interparticle forces, hydrodynamic interactions, and shear flow. Using parallelized Accelerated Stokesian Dynamics (PASD) simulations, we investigate cluster microstructure and rotational dynamics, and how their coupling produces suspension stress in sheared, attractive non-Brownian suspensions. When interparticle attraction dominates over separating shear forces, clusters grow until mechanical loading balances maximum interparticle bond strength. We examine how the cluster stresslet depends on cluster size, with both quantities normalized by their mechanical yielding scales. Scaled cluster stresslets collapse onto a master curve exhibiting three distinct regimes: cubic, quadratic, and linear with respect to the scaled radius of gyration $R_g$. In the cubic regime, small, compact clusters behave as rigid bodies, whose hydrodynamic stresslet scales with cluster volume $R_g^3$. As clusters grow into the quadratic regime, low-aspect-ratio clusters preferentially yield under flow, driving a proportional increase in average aspect ratio with size. High-aspect-ratio clusters follow Jeffery rotational dynamics within the flow-gradient plane, spending longer durations aligned with the flow and thereby reducing their time-averaged hydrodynamic stresslet to scale as $R_g^2$. In the linear regime, clusters approach the maximum size sustainable by the interparticle bonds. The internal tension is bounded by the maximum bond strength, limiting the stresslet to an $R_g$ dependence. These findings establish a mechanistic framework connecting microscale cluster morphology and dynamics to macroscale rheology.

papers.title: Simulations of a Conducting Sphere Moving through Magnetized Plasma II: Effect of Internal Magnetic Fields and Enhancement of Alfvénic Drag
papers.abstract: Magnetic interaction between astrophysical objects can play an important role and produce electromagnetic radiation in various systems, ranging from planet-moon and star-planet systems to binary compact objects. We extend our previous numerical study of an ideal magnetized plasma flowing past a conducting sphere to the case where the sphere is magnetized. Such a flow generates magnetic disturbances and produces a drag force on the sphere. We examine the drag coefficient as a function of the strength and orientation of the conductor's internal magnetic field relative to the background magnetic field. We find that a strong internal magnetic field that is aligned with the background field significantly enhances the drag coefficient compared to the unmagnetized case; this enhancement is related to the increased magnetic flux that connects the conductor and the open, external field region. We also explore how the drag coefficient changes as the flow transitions from the sub-Alfvénic to the super-Alfvénic regime. Our results suggest that magnetic interaction may play a larger role in orbital evolution of some binary systems than previously expected.

papers.title: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in foundation-model agents have enabled increasingly capable embodied systems for long-horizon planning and interaction. However, embodied agents require fast, closed-loop decisions as they continuously perceive and act on a changing environment. Deploying strong cloud agents leaves the platform idle for seconds between consecutive actions, while lightweight local models respond quickly but are more vulnerable to errors. Existing hierarchical architectures typically assign models fixed roles, whereas conventional model routers make stateless per-request decisions. We present CARE, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate control from a local executor to a stronger cloud model. A lightweight critic model monitors execution reliability and triggers escalation when local execution becomes unreliable; once escalated, control persists until the agent recovers, avoiding step-wise switching. To support such control transfer, a shared handoff memory maintains execution context and task-level progress across executors, enabling the model to intervene without restarting from scratch. Across diverse embodied benchmarks, CARE improves task success by 6.3-18.3 percentage points over the strongest evaluated collaboration baseline. CARE further approaches or exceeds Cloud-only success while reducing median time-between-action latency by 28.8-82.6%.

papers.title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems Are Vulnerable to Herding and Runaway Cascades
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate in multi-agent systems where they collaborate by responding to others' choices, creating endogenous feedback loops with vulnerability to social influence, herding behavior and runaway cascades. Following the design of the classic Music Lab experiment, we tested this vulnerability in large populations of LLM agents that recommended unfamiliar songs, with or without exposure to cumulative recommendation counts. Exposure led to runaway cascades that generated extreme and unpredictable collective recommendations increasingly divergent from a song's intrinsic appeal. Compared to humans, LLM populations were generally far more susceptible to herding behavior, and unlike humans, LLM cascades were less able to self-correct. This vulnerability has implications for multi-agent collaboration in recommender systems, automated evaluation, complex problem-solving, and unauthorized conspiracies.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: Objective: Iontophoretic drug delivery has primarily relied on current modulation to regulate drug transport. Here, we investigate hydrogel geometry, microstructure, and local electric fields as alternative mechanisms for controlling transdermal delivery. Methods: Bovine serum albumin (BSA) was encapsulated in polypyrrole-polyvinyl alcohol (PPy-PVA) hydrogels. Five geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs, were fabricated to vary pore architecture and local electric field distributions. We optimized PPy content, drug loading, and current density. Electric fields were evaluated using finite element analysis, and microstructures were characterized by scanning electron microscopy. Drug transport was assessed using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes. Results: Hydrogel geometries exhibited distinct microstructures and electric field distributions. Iontophoresis substantially enhanced permeability compared with passive diffusion, while individual geometries produced different cumulative release, flux, and permeability profiles. The average iontophoretic permeability was (3.80 +/- 1.93) x 10^-5, exceeding previously reported values using artificial membranes. Conclusion: Geometry-driven fabrication of drug-loaded hydrogels enables tunable transport characteristics under both iontophoretic and passive conditions. Significance: Geometry-mediated control offers an alternative approach to regulating iontophoretic drug delivery without requiring individual current-density modulation.

papers.title: Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals: Locally Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Prediction intervals from probabilistic time-series forecasters are commonly assessed by marginal coverage, the long-run proportion of observations falling inside the intervals. However, forecast errors in time series are often serially dependent and heteroskedastic, so prediction intervals can attain near-nominal marginal coverage while miscovering systematically during periods of larger local error variance. We identify and address this failure mode, which we call \emph{local scale miscalibration}. We first document the phenomenon using time-series foundation models (TSFMs): across several real-world series, their native intervals often attain near-nominal marginal coverage while exhibiting substantial temporal variation in local coverage, alternating between overcoverage and undercoverage over shorter windows. We then propose Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals (VCPI), a post-hoc calibration procedure that uses the base forecaster's predictive scale as a baseline, models the volatility of standardized forecast residuals with a Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) model, and applies a multiplicative correction to produce locally adaptive prediction intervals. We justify VCPI both theoretically and empirically, comparing it against model-agnostic conformal counterparts. We provide a theoretical analysis of interval adaptation of the proposed method following abrupt changes in volatility. Empirically, we evaluate VCPI on Chronos, Moirai, and TimesFM across four real-world datasets and find that it produces more stable local coverage than conformal baselines while maintaining near-nominal marginal coverage and comparable interval width.

papers.title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

papers.title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
papers.abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices, with $(n,m) = (1,1), (2,2)$ and $(2,4)$, from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. Charge transfer drives the system towards the V$^{4+}$ and Ni$^{2+}$ configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting $C$-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with $a^-b^+c^-$ or $a^-b^-c^-$ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a $d$-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)$_1$/(LNO)$_1$ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO$_3$, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen $2p$ states through $p$-$d$ covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a \textit{design} principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.

authors.name: Walber H. Brito

papers.title: Retraction-Free Nonsmooth Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold: Subgradient and Proximal Landing Methods
papers.abstract: We develop three retraction-free Landing methods for nonsmooth composite optimization over the Stiefel manifold, combining an (approximately) tangential direction with an infeasibility-reducing normal direction. The subgradient Landing method, with normal stepsizes parameterized by $α\in[0,1]$, has best-iterate complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$ for surrogate stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2/(2-α)})$ for feasibility. For $α=0$, it converges locally $R$-linearly under local weak sharpness and mild assumptions. The proximal gradient Landing method computes a tangential direction by solving a proximal subproblem and combines it with the same normal direction. Moreover, the inexact proximal gradient Landing method allows the proximal subproblem to be solved approximately and applies an explicit correction to control violations of the tangency condition. Both proximal methods have outer-iteration complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ for stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-1})$ for feasibility, and every accumulation point is first-order stationary. Under an additional asymptotic Bregman-error condition and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of a suitable auxiliary function, the primal sequence of the inexact method converges to a first-order stationary point. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of all three methods. On the tested sparse principal component analysis instances, the inexact method has favorable running times, and both proximal methods maintain small feasibility residuals.

papers.title: MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback
papers.abstract: Mix-policy optimization incorporates off-policy expert data into the reinforcement learning (RL) loop to transcend the capability boundary of on-policy RL. However, existing methods either provide static full-trace guidance that suppresses self-exploration, or adopt expert prefix guidance without correctness guarantees, leading to suboptimal performance or even training collapse. In this paper, we propose MOER, a mix-policy optimization framework that harmonizes expert guidance with self-exploration. MOER injects a decaying expert chain-of-thought prefix into the prompt and lets the model complete the remaining reasoning, with the prefix length progressively annealed to encourage self-exploration. A selective rollback mechanism replaces failed completions with the original full expert trace, guaranteeing the correctness of every off-policy trajectory. Furthermore, a harmonized mix-policy objective optimizes on-policy tokens with a GRPO loss while supervising both expert prefix and completion tokens with a trust-region SFT loss, substantially stabilizing training. Extensive experiments show that MOER achieves the highest average scores in mathematical and general domain reasoning tasks, outperforming all basic and mix-policy baselines, and generalizes consistently across diverse tasks, model scales, and base model categories. Codes are available at https://github.com/CityU-MLO/MOER.

papers.title: Astro2Method: Benchmarking LLMs on Machine Learning Method Selection in Astronomy
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in astronomy, but choosing a suitable method for a scientific problem often requires expertise in both astronomy and ML. Large language models (LLMs) could help astronomers make such choices, yet this ability remains underexplored in existing benchmarks. We introduce Astro2Method, a benchmark of 500 expert-reviewed binary questions from 346 astronomy papers (2024/01-2026/06), based on clear performance differences and complete (Easy) or partial (Hard) explanations from the authors. Across five LLMs, direct prompting achieves 87.50-92.55% accuracy on Easy questions but only 58.87-64.52% on Hard. Using historical papers, neither retrieval-augmented generation nor most agent methods with additional reasoning or retrieval (including ReAct, Self-Ask, and CRITIC) bring consistent improvement. Agents required to search the web improve accuracy mainly when they find the papers the questions are based on, with no consistent improvement otherwise. Providing the source paper's pipeline description with method names masked improves Hard accuracy, matching or exceeding web search. Together, these results suggest that relevant experimental information helps distinguish ML methods, but inferring it from related studies and domain knowledge remains challenging for LLMs in astronomy.

papers.title: On the Open Problem in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition
papers.abstract: We prove that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ not a perfect square, the only pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ for which there exists $r \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $r^a + \sqrt{n}$ and $r^b + \sqrt{n}$ are both rational numbers are those of the form $\{a, a\}$ or $\{g, 2g\}$ (with $g$ odd). This resolves an open question presented in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition.

papers.title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions. However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor. We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge. Extensive experiments, including benchmarking against 21 methods across 5 heterogeneity settings on 3 datasets and comprehensive ablation studies, validate the effectiveness of FedGRC. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, FedGRC surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in global recognition and personalization floors by at least 2.17% and 2.13%, respectively. On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.

authors.name: Junyu Lin
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
papers.abstract: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation. Meanwhile, transcription and replication continuously generate DNA supercoiling, yet how the resulting torsional stress affects co-condensation remains poorly understood. Here, by coupling DNA elasticity to a protein concentration field, we show that supercoiling acts as a topological catalyst for co-condensation through a mutually reinforcing interplay with protein wetting. Specifically, protein wetting facilitates twist-to-writhe conversion, generating highly writhed DNA conformations that in turn promote capillary collapse into a protein-rich droplet. In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation. These results establish topology as a distinct control parameter for biomolecular condensation and provide a mechanical framework for how active genomic processes can dynamically regulate large-scale genome organization.

authors.name: Sihan Liu
authors.institution: Fourth Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
papers.abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

authors.name: Minxuan Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving
papers.abstract: KV caching reduces the serving cost of large language models (LLMs), but the growing KV cache footprint is increasingly exceeds GPU and host-memory capacity. Therefore, people use SSD to expand the KV cache storage capacity with high I/O bandwidth. However, in production LLM workload, such as multi-round conversation and LLM agents, the total amount of KV cache writes significantly exceeds SSD capacity, shortening SSD lifetime from years to months. To improve SSD lifetime, a natural solution is to reduce the KV cache writes by gating the KV cache writes via historical access patterns. However, that significantly lowers the KV cache hit rate (and increase the LLM serving cost) since KV caches from different attention types might have identical historical access pattern but different future access patterns. Our insight is that, to reduce KV cache writes without hurting KV cache hit rate, one need to not only consider the access pattern, but also application-level information such as the attention type of KV cache. Leveraging this observation, we propose Gandalf , the first SSD KV cache offloading system with SSD life time awareness. Gandalf prioritize the admission of full-attention KV cache into SSD over the cache generated by other types of attention, which significantly increases SSD lifetime without sacrificing cache hit rate. Our evaluation shows that Gandalf extends the SSD lifetime by 7.3X on average, while having negligible impact on cache hit rate across multiple workload traces and wide range of hardware capacity. Gandalf design can be extended to other flash-based storage, such as High Bandwidth Flash (HBF).

papers.title: DConstrain: Compiling Context-Parameterized Transitions for Diffusion Language Model Constrained Decoding
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) decode multiple tokens in parallel, so individually valid tokens can be incompatible together under a schema. Exact joint inference over a grammar graph enforces compatibility, but it requires token-labeled successors across many hypothetical parser configurations. Encoding stacks and field histories in compiled states can cause exponential growth, which forces prior exact decoders to fix property orders and exclude valid outputs. We present DConstrain, which compiles schemas into context-parameterized transition programs. Cold compilation specializes token consumption to local grammar states while retaining context-dependent stack operations, environment guards, and caller-dependent deferred parsing symbolically. Tracking field histories as runtime values supports arbitrary property order without enumerating field subsets offline. At runtime, warm compilation binds reached configurations to these programs to construct exact successors, overlapping with the model forward pass because graph construction requires no model scores. Furthermore, token-effect grouping merges tokens with identical compiled effects before runtime contexts are bound, so groups are reused across stacks and environments even when concrete successors differ. Objective-specific score aggregation and token restoration provably preserve both the Viterbi optimum and the token-labeled path distribution of ungrouped inference. Across three benchmarks and two DLM families, DConstrain compiles 100% of BFCL schemas under arbitrary property orders, whereas an optimized finite-state baseline compiles only 71.30-85.81%. Under arbitrary property order, it reduces BFCL end-to-end decoding latency by 6.65-46.26 times with 100% schema validity and raises DiffusionGemma's BFCL accuracy from 37.27% under fixed order to 81.56%.

papers.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can perform a broad range of tasks across diverse settings, yet their performance in agentic contexts remains poorly understood. Although online evaluations in simulators and real-world environments are essential for measuring interactive agent performance, they are costly and challenging to scale. Complementary offline VQA benchmarks can enable faster and more reliable comparisons across agentic domains, yet existing benchmarks remain limited and fragmented. To address this gap, we introduce AgentVQA, an offline benchmark for evaluating VLMs on realistic agentic scenarios across five agent domains: Web Agents, Robotics, Egocentric Videos, Games, and Spatial Planning. We build AgentVQA by manually selecting 1000 challenging, real-world agent examples from 23 source datasets and adapting them for reliable offline evaluation. The resulting benchmark preserves realistic scenarios from interactive environments across diverse domains, and its model rankings track those from corresponding online evaluations. Across the 22 evaluated models, the best achieves only 58.5% accuracy. Our cross-domain analysis shows that errors are driven primarily by failures to ground and maintain accurate representations of the current and evolving visual state, including localizing relevant UI elements, interpreting motion, tracking state changes over time, and inferring 3D spatial relationships, rather than by task misinterpretation or downstream logical reasoning.

papers.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
papers.abstract: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech synthesized via a multi-speaker, dual-engine TTS pipeline; Stage 2 explores Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with transcription and script rewards. We find that synthetic SFT provides the primary cross-domain transfer to spontaneous human speech, reducing Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40% to 21.52% (-1.88 pp) and switch-point error rate (SPER) from 35.89% to 28.77% (-7.12 pp). Subsequent GRPO yields small, statistically significant adjustments on 173 test utterances (1.69%), driving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45% to 6.36% (p <= 0.001) and SPER to 28.70% (p = 0.022 clustered). Crucially, ablation reveals that in this SFT-converged encoder-decoder setting, an auxiliary script reward term yields performance identical to MER-only optimization because rollout candidate groups exhibit near-zero script variance on synthetic data. On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp (stabilizing at 18.42% after GRPO, a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while preserving English lexical WER (3.38% vs. 3.33%). Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.

papers.title: Padding to k: A Minimum Count in the Schema Makes Open-Weight Models Pad Their Extraction Lists
papers.abstract: Extraction pipelines ask language models for JSON that follows a schema, and the schema can set a minimum number of list entries. We ask what models do when the document holds fewer items than that minimum. Under a preregistered plan, we test eight open-weight models on 558 real documents from nine annotated datasets, with six more models on hosted services as a reference. Three findings stand out. First, models treat the count as a target: a minimum shown in the schema, but not enforced, raises the share of lists longer than the true count from 34.5% to 55.4%. Second, the padding is hard to catch, because most added entries are real text taken from the document; about half of them pass a check that each entry occurs in the source. Third, common fixes help only partly: a line saying fewer items are fine removes the effect on average but misses more true items, a count in prose ("up to k") also raises over-counting, an "N/A" option under an enforced minimum still leaves half the lists padded, and re-asking with the validation error makes padding far more common. We release the code, answer lists and run records at https://github.com/AbhishekBarali/padding-to-k

papers.title: Learned smoothing in operator-adapted multigrid: controlled accuracy gains and computational limits
papers.abstract: Learned multigrid components are often evaluated at a fixed iteration budget, but such comparisons do not distinguish local approximation gains from practical solver efficiency. We study this distinction for high-contrast elliptic problems on unstructured finite element meshes. A learned V-cycle uses operator-dependent transfers, Galerkin coarse operators, near-kernel deflation and an energy-norm safeguard; only its smoothers are trained. The architecture represents a specified class of fixed polynomial smoothers and is positively homogeneous in the load. On fresh conductive-channel problems, one learned pass reduces the energy error by factors of 5.7-6.1 relative to the same cycle with four-step Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate-gradient smoothing; the corresponding factors are 1.38-1.45 for insulating barriers. In a separate fixed-input test on channel problems, the fine-level learned smoother attains a smaller energy-norm error than the exact minimum over a five-dimensional Krylov space of its own input on 97-100 of 100 fresh inputs for each position and training initialization; this does not establish superiority over all polynomial-smoothed cycles. When the classical smoothing budget is increased, the paired geometric-mean accuracy crosses that of the learned cycle between 8 and 14 steps per smoothing call on channels and between 5 and 8 on barriers. The measured CPU implementation offers no computational advantage over the tested classical solvers, and load changes and floating islands further restrict its accuracy.

papers.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
papers.abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.

papers.title: Atlas: Making Sense of Long Horizon Agent Trajectories
papers.abstract: AI agents can now search literature, generate hypotheses, analyze datasets, and run experiments at a scale difficult for researchers to match. Yet scaling scientific execution does not automatically scale researchers' ability to make sense of what agents produce. When researchers return to a long-horizon run, they must evaluate work they did not monitor: what the agent produced, which decisions shaped those outputs, and whether those decisions served the research goal. We frame this post-run sensemaking as a representation problem across three linked levels: goal, decision, and artifact. From this framework we developed Atlas, an agentic workspace with a trajectory tree, which renders the run as a branching structure showing what the agent chose and set aside, and artifact projections over six representations. In a within-subjects study (N=14), participants reported higher decision transparency, artifact sensemaking, and goal connection with Atlas than with a standard baseline, together with substantially lower subjective workload.

papers.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
papers.abstract: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.

papers.title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
papers.abstract: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.

papers.title: Gender, Sexual Orientation, and the One-Year Refugee Bar: A Computational Study of Bill C-12 and Canadian Refugee Adjudication
papers.abstract: In March 2026, Bill C-12 amended the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act to make refugee claims ineligible for referral to the Refugee Protection Division where they are made more than one year after the claimant's first entry to Canada. Affected claimants are diverted to a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA), which is typically decided by an immigration officer on a paper record, with no guaranteed oral hearing, no appeal on the merits, and no automatic stay of removal pending judicial review. The government defended the bar partly on the premise that genuine refugees claim promptly. Critics countered that late claims are concentrated among vulnerable groups, particularly people fleeing persecution based on gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression (SOGIE). This article tests those competing premises. Using artificial intelligence tools, checked through human review, it examines nearly 29,000 published decisions of the Refugee Protection Division, the Refugee Appeal Division, and the Federal Court from 2006 to 2025. The results of this study demonstrate that, first, while most claimants claim within a year, roughly one in nine in the published record does not, and gender and SOGIE claims are significantly overrepresented among these late claims. Second, among late claims, refusals of gender and SOGIE claims are more likely than refusals of other claims to be overturned on appeal or judicial review. Late claims on other grounds, by contrast, fare somewhat worse on review than timely claims. The one-year bar therefore removes the hearing, the appeal, and the stay from the late claimants for whom those safeguards have been doing the most work. The article recommends repealing the bar or, failing that, adopting exemptions, procedural protections, and greater transparency in PRRA decision making.

papers.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
papers.abstract: When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing. Runtime overlays normalize native observations, while a deterministic pipeline joins invocation and result lifecycles, constructs a typed provenance graph, selects a policy-decisive slice, and binds claims to recorded evidence. Given the same normalized trace, overlay version, and pre-run policy oracle, the diagnosis can be recomputed and its claims re-checked without language-model judgment. Across five runtimes, one contract captures all 159 applicable executions, with an audit of native and synthesized identifiers. On 120 adjudicated cases, AgentTriage achieves 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate, improving joint diagnosis by 0.175 (95% CI [0.092, 0.258]) over the strongest same-schema baseline. These results quantify the precision of replayable diagnosis and the observation boundaries that require abstention. We release an open-source implementation and selected sanitized evidence at https://github.com/AsnGs/agenttriage-open-source.

papers.title: AgentPhishing: A Benchmark of LLM Email Agents Under Adaptive Attack
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents increasingly handle private information and act on users' behalf across desktop and web applications, including email. Phishing therefore poses privacy and security risks that depend not only on whether agents recognize malicious messages, but also on how they respond. Existing phishing datasets were developed primarily for conventional detection, leaving agent susceptibility to persuasive malicious requests insufficiently characterized. To expose vulnerabilities that pre-existing datasets may miss, we introduce AgentPhishing, a benchmark for evaluating whether persuasive phishing attacks can evade detection and induce LLM email agents to comply with malicious requests. We develop PhishOpt, which optimizes reusable email-generation skills against individual agents under fixed benchmark constraints and a realism constraint. We analyze the generated emails using Cialdini's persuasion principles to identify strategies associated with agent failures and use these findings to construct a universal generation skill. Our evaluation shows that agents can handle pre-existing phishing emails safely yet remain susceptible to attacks adapted to agent behavior, while in an AgentPhishing evaluation of nine agents, four exhibit phishing-detection rates below $10\%$ and malicious-request compliance rates above $45\%$. These results highlight the limits of inferring agent safety from conventional phishing evaluations and the need to assess how agents respond to persuasive malicious requests.

authors.name: Miao Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
papers.abstract: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.

authors.name: Hanxuan Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Quantitative constructive representation of the KdV flow in $H^3$ via $L^2$-energy-preserving centered-difference Chernoff approximations and Picard iteration
papers.abstract: We give a constructive representation of the solution of the KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6uu_x$ on $\mathbb R$ for real initial data in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. The approximations couple an exact, unitary centered-difference Chernoff product for the Airy group with a skew-symmetric discretization of the quadratic term, and are computed by Picard iteration; they preserve the $L^2$ norm exactly, as does the limit. A two-mesh Cauchy argument shows that the whole sequence converges in $C([0,T];H^2)$, at rate $O(n^{-\frac{2(s-2)}5})$ for $H^s$ data ($3\leq s\leq 7$), and in $L^2$ at rate $O(n^{-6/5})$ for $H^3$ data. This scheme, to the best of our knowledge, is novel and is of independent interest. As a by-product we obtain existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, Lipschitz dependence on the data in the $H^2$ norm, uniformly on bounded subsets of $H^3$ and compact time intervals, and joint locally Lipschitz dependence of $(t,f)\mapsto S(t)f$ into $L^2$; the classical conservation laws extend the flow globally in time.

papers.title: xVGAE: A Hierarchical Variational Graph Autoencoder for Exchangeable Graphs
papers.abstract: Graphs play a crucial role in many applications, ranging from drug discovery to social network modeling and astronomy. Generative models for graphs have substantially advanced in recent years, but we identify relatively simple scenarios where state-of-the-art models struggle to converge within a standard compute budget, or exhibit prohibitively slow generation times. We propose a generative architecture that achieves quality competitive with state-of-the-art models and is orders of magnitude faster at generation. Our approach is inspired by the Aldous-Hoover theorem, a classic representation theorem that characterizes any probability distribution of graphs that is invariant to permutations of node indices or exchangeable. This theorem establishes that three ingredients suffice: a graph-level latent variable, a set of exchangeable node-specific latent variables, and a so-called graphon function that maps graph- and node-level variables to the probability of an edge between any node pair. Given a training set of graphs, our exchangeable Variational Graph AutoEncoder (xVGAE) learns an approximation to their underlying graphons, as well as graph- and node-level latent variables. We show that our xVGAE encodes latent representations that correlate with graph- and node-level properties, and can (quickly, in one shot) generate new graphs that closely match key training set statistics.

papers.title: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps have emerged as a key spatial memory representation for long-horizon robot autonomy, enabling robots to reason about objects, their spatial relationships, and past observations across time. However, existing object-centric semantic maps are primarily designed for static environments and rely on an append-only point integration strategy, where newly observed points are accumulated but previously integrated points are rarely reevaluated. Consequently, perception errors accumulate over time, and outdated points persist after objects move or disappear. Although recent dynamic mapping methods update object-level representations in changing scenes, they do not explicitly revise noisy or obsolete points within each object. We propose an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating. Each object point maintains a confidence score that is updated online using multi-view temporal evidence: consistent observations reinforce reliable points, while inconsistent segmentation masks, depth measurements, and visibility cues suppress spurious and outdated points. Combined with object tracking and re-identification to preserve instance identities under motion and relocation, our framework enables object-centric semantic maps to be continuously refined rather than monotonically accumulated. Experiments demonstrate improved mapping accuracy over the previous method by 3.46% on Replica and 2.55% on ScanNet, show robustness in dynamic environments and under perception noise, and provide an effective spatial memory for object navigation and embodied question-answering with success rates of 82.4% and 76.7%.

authors.name: Taimeng Fu
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Zitong Zhan
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Shaoshu Su
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Chen Wang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: On the Concordance Invariants of Cable Links
papers.abstract: We study the Beliakova--Wehrli link $s$-invariant and Cavallo's link $τ$-invariant of coherently oriented cables. For knots satisfying extremal four-ball genus and maximal self-linking hypotheses, we establish bounds for the $s$-invariant of $(p,q)$-cables, where $p$ and $q$ are not necessarily coprime, and show that these bounds are sharp under certain conditions. For the $τ$-invariant, we prove analogous bounds for arbitrary companion knots and exact formulas whenever $τ(K)=\pm g_4(K)\ne 0$. Specializing to the coherently oriented cable links associated to an $n$-framed knot, we apply these bounds to the lasagna $s$-invariant of Ren and Willis. The resulting applications provide upper bounds for the lasagna $s$-invariant of knot traces and a criterion for distinguishing homeomorphic zero traces up to orientation-preserving diffeomorphism.

authors.name: Aadhishwaran Bhuvaraghamoorthy
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Two-Timescale Antenna Positioning for Pinching-Antenna System Based on Statistical Channel Information
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a two-timescale antenna position optimization framework for the pinching-antenna system (PASS). The proposed framework exploits statistical channel state information (CSI) to determine large-timescale pinching-antenna (PA) positions over the entire waveguide, and utilizes instantaneous CSI to refine PA positions at the small timescale within a local region. This approach effectively captures the benefits of large-timescale PA positioning for long-term system performance and small-timescale PA movement for real-time adaptation to fast channel fluctuations. For the single-user case, we derive closed-form solutions for the optimal large-timescale PA positions, and further analyze a performance upper bound together with the conditions for achieving this bound, which guide the small-timescale position refinement. For the multi-user case, an upper bound on the minimum rate among all users is derived. To maximize their minimum rate, we develop an element-wise search algorithm for large-timescale PA positioning and a projected gradient ascent method for small-timescale position refinement. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme closely approaches the derived bounds and consistently outperforms conventional schemes by reducing path loss via large-timescale PA positioning and suppressing inter-user interference through small-timescale local movement.

authors.name: Zijian Zhou
authors.institution: National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering

papers.title: Data-Driven Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing: A Survey
papers.abstract: During the deep learning era, innovations in remote sensing (RS) vision models primarily focused on optimizing network architectures for specific tasks and conducting end-to-end training. However, with the advent of the Vision-Language Models (VLMs) era, constrained by substantial computational resource demands, the mainstream research paradigm has shifted towards adapting general-purpose VLMs using RS vertical domain data for fine-tuning, rather than modifying their core architectures. This transition marks a change in the innovation pathway from model-centric to data-centric. Despite the increasing importance of data, the academic community still lacks a systematic, data-centric survey to guide researchers in constructing high-quality RS vision-language datasets for various application scenarios and in conducting effective model fine-tuning and performance evaluation based on these datasets. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic review of the development status of RS datasets tailored for VLMs. It further provides a comprehensive practical guide for RS researchers in the large model era, covering the entire pipeline from data construction to fine-tuning and evaluation. This paper aims to encourage the academic community to build more diverse and higher-quality vision-language datasets for specialized RS sub-fields. Ultimately, the goal is to converge these efforts into a comprehensive RS vision-language corpus that offers extensive task coverage and a wide geographical distribution, thereby laying a solid data foundation for advancing towards general artificial intelligence in RS.

authors.name: Xue Yang
authors.institution: Guizhou University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
papers.abstract: Autonomous research agents are increasingly used to automate large portions of scientific research, yet they are prone to research integrity violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of the research process. We present RIDAR, a framework for automated RIV detection and runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT, a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types spanning the full research lifecycle. Building on RIVT, we present RIDAR-post-hoc, a framework to detect RIVs within agent trajectories. RIDAR-post-hoc achieves 85.2% F1 performance on RIV-Gold, a benchmark for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated trajectories. Applying RIDAR-post-hoc to RIV-Wild, a dataset of 300 agent trajectories across 50 distinct research tasks, we detect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajectories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in current agents. Finally, we present RIDAR-runtime, a framework for dynamically detecting and correcting RIVs during agent runtime. RIDAR-runtime effectively reduces agent RIVs remaining at task completion by 36.8%. We will release our code and data to facilitate future research.

papers.title: Stochastic Geometry Analysis and Optimization for Multi-LEO Satellite-Assisted Communications
papers.abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are vital in providing seamless connectivities to ground users (GUs). However, complex satellite-to-ground propagation and non-negligible satellite failure probabilities make single-satellite transmission unreliable. To address this issue, we consider a multi-LEO-satellite communication network (mLEO-CN), where a typical GU is served by multiple LEO satellites. The satellite locations are modeled as a binomial point process on a sphere and ordered according to their distances to the GU. To improve communication reliability, a serial communication scheme is adopted, in which the subsequent satellite is activated only when all preceding satellites fail to satisfy the target signal-to-noise ratio threshold. By employing the tool of stochastic geometry, we derive key performance metrics, including overall transmission success probability, average transmission rate, and end-to-end delay under the serial communication scheme by incorporating both shadowed Rician (SR) fading and satellite failure probabilities. To improve analytical tractability, we derive asymptotic expressions for the end-to-end transmission success probability in two special cases by leveraging the asymptotic expression of the SR fading model and a Gamma-distribution, and further propose a cluster-based approximation approach for the overall transmission success probability. Building on these analyses, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the ratio of the overall transmission success probability to the end-to-end delay, and obtain its solution using a one-dimensional search approach. Numerical results validate the analysis, reveal the impact of key parameters, and identify the optimal number of serving LEO satellites under different constellation altitudes.

papers.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
papers.abstract: Does computing a composition of total Boolean functions require the product of the randomized query complexities of its factors? We give a negative answer. There are families of total functions $f,g$ such that $R(f\circ g) =Θ\!\left(\frac1{\log R(g)}\right)R(f)R(g)$ This result requires first separating linearized query complexity $\LR$, as well as noisy randomized query complexity $noisyR$, from standard randomized query complexity $R$. Both constructions essentially come from totalizing existing partial function separations, albeit via different techniques. By adapting these techniques, we also construct total functions separating every adjacent pair in the chain from sabotage $RS$, max-conflict $\barχ$, and linearised query complexity $LR$. We show that AND-of-ORs separates conflict $χ$ from max-conflict $\barχ$ complexity and makes conflict and sabotage incomparable. Finally, randomized complexity can be smaller than its composition limit $R^*$ by the maximal factor $Θ(\log R)$. The total--total composition separation is also formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.

authors.name: Ryan Mc Gowan
authors.institution: United States Army Combat Capabilities Development Command

papers.title: The Limits of Price Discrimination When the Market Is Unknown
papers.abstract: Bergemann, Brooks, and Morris (2015) characterize the consumer and producer surplus pairs that segmentation can produce when the distribution of values is known. I fix only the set of possible values and characterize the pairs that some market and some segmentation can produce. They form a convex polygon. Its outer edge is the largest efficient surplus a market can have when its uniform-price profit is capped, net of that profit, and truncated equal-revenue markets attain it. At the values no segmentation is needed; strictly between two values, reaching the frontier requires splitting a market into two extremal markets. With a continuum of values up to $\bar{v}$, consumer surplus is at most $π\ln(\bar{v}/π)$ when producer surplus (the seller's profit) is $π$, this bound is reached without segmentation, and no market gives consumers more than $\bar{v}/e$.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
papers.abstract: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup. Because the random mapping is not learned from language, its prompts can be highly unnatural, and as such easily detectable through input guardrails, and the risk estimates they yield are not grounded in natural prompts. In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure. We evaluate this approach under two settings: sampling-based estimation using \emph{RareTrap} and optimization-based search using \emph{ThinkTrap}. We find that character-level perplexity drops from $10^3$--$10^7$ to 3--5 in RareTrap and from 20--28 to 4.3--5.4 in ThinkTrap. We also find that model risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude across the two mappings.

papers.title: SnakeCharmer: Orchestrating Utility, Timeliness, and Placement in GPU Prefetching
papers.abstract: GPUs rely on massive thread-level parallelism to tolerate long memory latency, yet they still suffer severe stalls when many warps simultaneously wait for data from the memory system. Address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers can mitigate such stalls, but accurate prediction alone does not guarantee performance improvement: a predicted prefetch becomes beneficial only if it is worth issuing, arrives at the right time, and is retained without harmful interference. Because these requirements interact, optimizing any single dimension in isolation can simply move the bottleneck to another. We capture these requirements with a predicted-prefetch-to-realized-benefit perspective and propose SnakeCharmer, a unified backend prefetch-control framework for address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers. SnakeCharmer separates address prediction from prefetch realization: the frontend predictor generates prefetch candidates, while the backend control path jointly controls utility, timeliness, and placement by determining whether each candidate should be issued, when it should be issued, and where the returned data should be retained. SnakeCharmer realizes this control path with zero-value-aware filtering for utility, hierarchical feedback-driven distance tuning for timeliness, and a register-assisted prefetch buffer for placement. We design and implement SnakeCharmer primarily on top of Snake, and adapt the same backend-control principles to APOGEE to demonstrate that SnakeCharmer's benefits are not limited to a single frontend predictor. On an A100 GPU model, SnakeCharmer improves performance/energy efficiency by 12.8%/20.8% over Snake and by 1.7%/3.2% over APOGEE, with modest hardware overhead.
