The map in (2) is of interest in representation theory due to recent developments in tensor-triangular geometry. To understand representations of a finite self-injective Hopf algebra AA over a Noetherian commutative ring RR, we can pass to the stable module category of RR-lattices, stmod⁡(A,R)\operatorname{stmod}(A,R). This has the structure of a finite monoidal triangulated category, and if AA is cocommutative, then it is a (symmetric) tensor triangulated category [7]. With this structure, we can attempt to classify thick tensor ideals—thick subcategories closed under tensor products, finite sums, and triangles—as a way of understanding the representation structure of AA. The results of this paper are applicable to Hopf algebras defined over the cyclotomic integers ℤ⁡[ζ]⊂ℂ\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]\subset\mathbb{C} for ζ\zeta an ℓ\ellth root of unity. The key property of this ring is that every nonzero prime ideal contains a positive integer. This allows us to first pass to a ring of positive characteristic. We call a ring with such property a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-saturated domain. Section 2 of the paper explores rings with this property, and Section 3 gives some important examples of Hopf algebras over ℤ\mathbb{Z}-saturated domains coming from Nichols algebras.

Nichols algebras are a unifying construction for a braided Hopf algebra that produces many well-known algebras, including the symmetric and exterior algebras and quantum groups. Nichols algebras arose independently in multiple different contexts. More recently, Nicholás Andruskiewitsch and Hans-Jürgen Schneider produced a method of lifting diagonal Nichols algebras as a way of classifying finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebras [3]. István Heckenberger classified all finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of diagonal type in [17], which give rise to these Hopf algebras. The main theorem of our paper is motivated in part as a potential tool for Hopf algebras arising in this way. Section 4 gives our main theorem.

papers.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
papers.abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every bijective non-contractive self-map has the following structure: the quasi-metric splits as $d = λ^- + D_0$. The invariant limit register $λ^-$ is a quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which the map is an isometry, with totally bounded symmetrization on every orbit, so that the map's rigid shadow is a rotation of a compact monothetic group; the asymmetric limit structure on it, a priori only paratopological, carries the compact topology. The defect $D_0$ lies in a band between a past fee difference and the fee of its source, the fee nondecreasing along orbits and vanishing in the deep past. The defect is zero precisely when the map is an isometry. Deep sources are thus almost rigid: in the deep past the map is an isometry to within any $\varepsilon$, against every target. Every such map that is not an isometry is a toll over its rigid shadow, levied on a forward-invariant zone that sheds into the past. Two further facts are forced: the orbit of the source of any strict pair is infinite and already strict, and the source pays its whole defect on its own backward returns, uniformly on a chain-closed set of displacements. The band is attained at both ends, and beyond it the shape of the defect is not forced: three spirals over the circle show that the toll can depend on the target, that a source carrying a fee can descend for free, and that an ascent can carry defect; no rate of shedding is forced either, and for zone tolls (two-valued descent tolls that are shift-monotone and subadditive along their own routes) the fee reaches zero already at a finite depth, by the ascending chain condition on submonoids of $\mathbb{N}$. The results are machine-checked in Lean, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

The fee always vanishes in the deep past (Section 7): if every point of a backward orbit kept a fee, stepping backward one fee-carrying near-return at a time, with tolerances shrinking geometrically, would produce a sequence whose every forward pair is expensive, against (i). Deep sources are thus almost rigid: far enough back on any orbit, every defect out of a point is small. Under hereditary precompactness alone, every non-contractive bijection is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits. The rate is not forced, since the height spiral’s fee is positive at every depth; for zone tolls (two-valued descent tolls that are shift-monotone and subadditive along their own routes), which include the toll spiral, the fee reaches zero already at a finite depth, by the ascending chain condition on submonoids of ℕ\mathbb{N}. Combined with the fee bound, the vanishing answers the classification question of [6] structurally: every non-isometric non-contractive bijection is a toll over its rigid shadow, levied on a forward-invariant zone that sheds into the past (Theorem 1.1).
